key_insight: Scaling humanoid Behavior Foundation Models works best when the learning paradigm, data strategy, and architecture are co-designed around whole-body motion tracking in a global frame.
engineering_relevance: The paper offers a practical recipe for building more general and controllable humanoid robots that can transfer better across tasks and environments in both simulation and real-world settings.
method: Reformulate humanoid control as global-frame whole-body motion tracking.
Balance on-policy rollout quantity with diverse reference motions.
Use the Humanoid Transformer to learn structured behavioral representations at scale.
evidence_signal: Extensive simulation and real-world experiments report over 10% lower MPKPE in local mode and 82% lower MPKPE in global mode versus existing humanoid controllers.
watch_item: The scaling gains depend on carefully coordinating data diversity, rollout collection, and model design, so weaker alignment across these components may reduce performance.
paper_title: Scaling Behavior Foundation Model for Humanoid Robots
